title: From Followers to Donors
text:
The problem


A small equine-therapy nonprofit relies on donations to keep care affordable, but has very little staff time for marketing.
GA4 went live in October 2026. The director’s question:

Which visitors are worth our limited time, and why aren’t they reaching the donation page?








Audience


Executive Director, who decides where marketing effort goes.









Data


GA4 · Sep 18 – Oct 15, 2026 · aggregated, no personal data





Frame this as a resource-allocation question, not a traffic question.

title: From Followers to Donors
text:
But does that traffic engage?












Chi-square test of independence
χ² = 22.96, df = 2, p < .001
Engagement does depend on the source.
Pairwise (Bonferroni):

Instagram vs. direct: p < .001
Other pairs: not significant at this sample size

title: From Followers to Donors
text:
Engaged, but briefly
Instagram has the highest engagement rate but the shortest visits (26s). Google organic visitors stay the longest (56s).

title: From Followers to Donors
text:
Where attention is lost
The homepage gets about half of all views but holds visitors only 12 seconds, and no donation page made the top 10.

title: From Followers to Donors
text:
Mobile-first, no question













88% of users are on mobile (87.6% per GA4)
Mobile engagement rate: 71.88%; desktop: 61.86%
Engagement rate differs by device: Fisher’s exact test, p = 0.029 (used because tablet counts are small)

Desktop visits run longer (79s), but mobile is where the audience is.

title: From Followers to Donors
text:
Recommendations

Make Instagram the primary donor channel. It’s the biggest, most engaged source. Add UTM-tagged donation links and a clear ask.
Fix the homepage first. Add impact stats and a visible Donate button above the fold, since half of all visitors land there.
Bring the donation pathway into the top 10. Link to it from Community Events and Volunteer, the pages supporters already spend time on.
Design mobile-first. Test every donation step on a phone.
Finish tracking. Set up completed donations as a key event so the next report measures dollars, not just clicks.

title: From Followers to Donors
text:
Limitations & next steps
Limitations

Only a few weeks of data, so results are an early baseline
GA4 is observational: results show associations, not causes
Average engagement time has no variance in standard reports, so it’s compared descriptively

Next steps

Refresh with later GA4 exports and compare before and after donor campaigns and the homepage redesign
Export raw events to BigQuery for session-level analysis
Add completed-donation tracking, then measure donation conversion rate by channel

title: Building My Personal Brand Website
text:
Why Style a Quarto Site?
Quarto sites look clean out of the box thanks to Bootstrap themes, but every site using the default theme looks the same. CSS and SCSS let you match your personal or client brand (colors, fonts, spacing) so the site feels like yours.






TipQuick definitions




CSS (Cascading Style Sheets): the language browsers use to style HTML (colors, fonts, layout).
SCSS (Sassy CSS): a superset of CSS that adds variables, nesting, and functions. Quarto compiles it into regular CSS when you render.

title: Building My Personal Brand Website
text:
SCSS Features Worth Knowing



Variables
Store a value once ($brand-green) and reuse it everywhere. Change it in one place to rebrand.




Nesting
Write &:hover inside .card-box instead of repeating the selector. It keeps related styles together.




Functions
lighten($brand-green, 15%) makes color variations on the fly, like the gradient in the demo box above.

title: Building My Personal Brand Website
text:
Light & Dark Mode
SCSS also makes a dark-mode toggle easy. Quarto adds the switch to the navbar automatically:


_quarto.yml

format:
  html:
    theme:
      light: [cosmo, custom.scss]
      dark:  [darkly, custom-dark.scss]

title: Building My Personal Brand Website
text:
Tips for Marketing Sites

Start with brand variables. Pull the client’s hex codes from their style guide into scss:defaults first.
Use $primary instead of hard-coding colors, so buttons and links stay consistent.
Keep custom classes reusable (.card-box, .skill) instead of styling one-off elements.
Check contrast. Brand gold on white can fail accessibility, so use it for accents and borders, not body text.
Inspect in the browser (right-click → Inspect) to find the exact selector you need to override.

title: Website Analytics
text:
BigQuery Analysis
Example query used to count sessions by traffic source from the GA4 export:


sessions_by_source.sql

SELECT
  traffic_source.source AS source,
  traffic_source.medium AS medium,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(user_pseudo_id,
        CAST((SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params)
              WHERE key = 'ga_session_id') AS STRING))) AS sessions
FROM `YOUR-PROJECT.analytics_YOUR-PROPERTY-ID.events_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20261101' AND '20261130'
GROUP BY source, medium
ORDER BY sessions DESC;

Hi, I’m Ron! I’m a graduate student in the Master of Science in Digital Marketing (MSDM) program at Cal Poly Pomona. I like working where data and storytelling meet: figuring out what the numbers say, then turning that into content people actually want to watch or read.
I work as a Social Media & Marketing Assistant at Associated Students, Inc. (ASI), creating content for accounts with 20K+ combined followers, and I’ve interned in marketing at Yamaha Corporation of America and the Ontario Jr Reign. Right now I’m also on an MSDM capstone team helping a nonprofit client, Wellness Ranch Therapy, use its website data to reach more supporters.

title: Ron Stephen Sabilla
text:
Personal Statement
I got into marketing through content: making videos, posts, and promo pieces that people actually stop and watch, from growing a junior hockey team’s social following to producing Reels for campus programs. Graduate school showed me the other half of the job. Good content is only as useful as your ability to prove what it did. Now I like working on both sides: setting up the tracking, finding what the data says, and turning it into the next piece of content or the next decision.
I’m especially drawn to mission-driven work. Helping a small nonprofit figure out which visitors turn into supporters has shown me how much a clear analysis can matter when time and budget are tight. I’m looking for a role in digital marketing analytics where I can keep connecting the creative and the measurable.

Wellness Ranch Therapy is a nonprofit in Rancho Cucamonga that offers equine-assisted therapy. Our team is helping them grow their reach and donations through website & SEO improvements, GA4 analytics, Google Ad Grants, and donor outreach. Here’s my part:

title: Traffic Source & AOV Analysis
text:
For our IBM 6540 (Applied Machine Learning for Marketing) group project, our five-person team analyzed a 60,000-row Shopify sales dataset. I owned RO1: traffic source and average order value (AOV) and wrote the conclusion slides.
Finding: No statistically significant overall difference in AOV between channels, but meaningful channel × category interaction effects. Some channels performed better for specific product categories.
Tools: R, recipes, rsample, glmnet, Quarto revealjs
